whatItDoes: Authorize up to $18 million in bonds for roofs, plumbing, dry rot, termite damage, electrical systems, safety and classrooms. Property taxes would repay principal and interest. The district estimates $1.3 million annually, an average rate of $30 and highest rate of $30 per $100,000 of assessed value, collection through fiscal 2062–63, and approximately $43,170,000 total repayment. These are projections, not guaranteed tax caps or repayment amounts. The district projects an extension of existing tax rates rather than an increase. Interest rates and bond terms must stay within legal limits. Money must stay local and fund the listed projects. Funds cannot pay teacher or administrator salaries or other school operating expenses. Independent citizen oversight and annual financial and performance audits are required. Some projects may depend on other funding, including state matching funds that are not guaranteed; not every listed project is guaranteed completion. Approval requires 55% of votes.
yesMeans: Authorize the district to borrow up to $18 million for the listed facilities and levy property taxes to repay the bonds under these conditions.
noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds through this measure.

parts.label: Charter facilities, workforce housing and prior tax limit
parts.what: The project list includes workforce housing for teachers and staff. It sets aside $567 million for charter-school facilities, adjustable by the board if the proportion of resident students attending charter schools changes; spending must consider a special committee with a majority of charter-community representatives. The 2008 Proposition S tax-rate limitation does not cover bonds approved through this later measure.
